# PSGraphToolbox Graph Toolkit - AI Coding Instructions

## Project Overview
PowerShell toolkit for Microsoft Entra ID operations via Microsoft Graph API. The only dependency is `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication` (`Invoke-MgGraphRequest`, `Connect-MgGraph`); custom wrappers add pagination, batching, delta sync and throttle handling.

**Core Philosophy**: Minimal dependencies, CLM-compatible, PowerShell 5.1+, pipeline-friendly.

---

## Repository Layout and Build

```
src/<category>/        # source of truth - one function per file, file name = function name
src/core/              # Invoke-GtGraphRequest, batch, delta sync, directory object lookup
src/core/helpers/      # helper functions (+ storageProviders/ for delta state persistence)
docs/<category>/       # GENERATED by platyPS - never edit by hand
tests/                 # Pester tests
utils/build.ps1        # build script
utils/functions|scripts/  # unrelated/WIP utilities, NOT part of the module
PsGraphToolbox.psm1/.psd1/.zip  # GENERATED - never edit by hand
```

- `utils\build.ps1 -ModuleVersion x.y.z` concatenates all `src/**/*.ps1` (sorted by path) into `PsGraphToolbox.psm1`, writes the `.psd1` manifest, generates docs with platyPS, runs the tests and zips the package. **It must be run in PowerShell 5.1** and needs a Graph connection (integration tests). When asked to change behavior, edit `src/` only.
- **Export rule**: every *top-level* `function Name` (no indentation, no `(` on the line) is exported - this includes the helpers (`isValidGuid`, `Write-GtVerbose`, ...). Functions nested inside another function (indented) are private. Never put a column-0 `function name(...)` line in PowerShell code unless it is JavaScript inside a here-string (see `Export-GtHtmlReport`).
- Doc category = the **immediate parent folder** of the file (e.g. `src/core/helpers/isValidGuid.ps1` -> `docs/helpers/`).
- Adding a function: new file in the matching `src/<category>/` folder, full comment-based help, add a README example/section if it is user-facing, and add/extend tests where practical.

---

## ⚠️ CRITICAL: PowerShell 5.1 Constrained Language Mode

**ALL code MUST work in PowerShell 5.1 Constrained Language Mode (CLM).**

### ❌ Prohibited
- Static .NET methods: `[System.IO.File]::ReadAllText()`, `[Guid]::Parse()`, `[DateTime]::UtcNow`
- `[PSCustomObject]@{}` - use `New-Object -TypeName PSObject` + `Add-Member` (or `New-Object PSObject -Property @{}`)
- `Add-Type`, `[scriptblock]::Create()`, COM objects (`New-Object -ComObject`), non-approved `New-Object` types
- `SupportsShouldProcess` / `$PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess` - not usable in CLM; use the custom `-WhatIf`/`-Confirm` pattern below
- PowerShell 7-only syntax (`??`, `?:`, `&&`, `ForEach-Object -Parallel`, ternary)

### ✅ Allowed / Safe Alternatives
- Type checks, casts to approved types and instance methods: `$x -is [datetime]`, `[guid]$RoleDefinitionId`, `[regex]$pattern`, `[array]`, `[int]`, `$date.ToLocalTime()`, `$date.ToString('o')`
- Operators over methods where possible:

```powershell
$text -replace "a", "b"          # Not: $text.Replace("a", "b")
$text -split ","                 # Not: $text.Split(",")
[System.Guid]$guid = $string     # Not: [Guid]::Parse($string)
Get-Date $string                 # Not: [DateTime]::Parse($string)
(Get-Date).ToUniversalTime()     # Not: [DateTime]::UtcNow
Get-Content -Path $path -Raw     # Not: [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText()

# object creation
$obj = New-Object -TypeName PSObject
$obj | Add-Member -NotePropertyName userId -NotePropertyValue $id

# HTML encoding
$text -replace "&","&amp;" -replace "<","&lt;" -replace ">","&gt;"
```

## ⚠️ AI-Generated Code Marking

**Mark ALL AI-generated code clearly**, naming the model used (see existing files, e.g. `Get-GtAgentIdentities`, `Export-GtHtmlReport`, `removeObjectIds`).

```powershell
# Entire function (inside comment-based help)
<#
.DESCRIPTION
[AI-GENERATED] This function was generated using Claude Opus 4.8.

Retrieves ...
Requires scopes: User.Read.All.
#>

# Code block
# [AI-GENERATED START] - Batch processing logic
$chunks = Split-ArrayIntoChunks -Enumerable $items -ChunkSize 20
# [AI-GENERATED END]

# Inline / small nested function
# [AI-GENERATED] returns a copy of the object tree without 'id' / '*Id' properties
```

Test files carry a header: `[AI-GENERATED] This file was generated using Claude Opus 4.5.`

## Architecture Quick Reference

### Core (`src/core/`)
- **`Invoke-GtGraphRequest`** - GET wrapper around `Invoke-MgGraphRequest`: auto-connect, auto-pagination, OData parameters, ConsistencyLevel header, delta support, UTC -> local dateTime conversion
- **`Invoke-GtGraphBatchRequest`** - `$batch` processor (20/batch), retries on 429 using `retry-after`, returns a **hashtable keyed by request `id`**. Uses `Invoke-GtGraphSingleBatchRequest` (one batch call) internally
- **`Sync-GtGraphResourceDelta`** - delta sync with persisted state (storage providers in `core/helpers/storageProviders/`)
- **`Get-GtGraphDirectoryObjectsByIds`** - bulk `getByIds` resolver (chunks of 1000). *Note: the file is named `Get-GtGraphDirectoryObjectByIds.ps1`, the function has `Objects`.*

### Helpers (`src/core/helpers/`) - all exported, used by every function
- **`Get-idFromInputObject`** (alias **`idFromInputObject`**) - normalizes UPN/GUID/object to `@{ id; type }` (`guid`/`upn`/`string`); `-objectIdOnly` requires a GUID, `-AllowRawString` allows display names
- **`isValidGuid`** / **`isValidUserPrincipalName`** - pipeline-friendly validators (lowerCamelCase, no `Gt` prefix)
- **`New-GtRequestUri`** - OData URI builder (used by `Invoke-GtGraphRequest`)
- **`Write-GtVerbose`** - timestamped `Write-Verbose`
- **`ConvertTo-GtLocalDateTime`** - recursive in-place UTC -> local conversion of dateTime values
- **`ConvertTo-HashTable`** - array -> hashtable keyed by `-keyProperty` (default `id`)
- **`Split-ArrayIntoChunks`** (alias `chunk`) - array chunking
- **`Export-GtHtmlReport`** - self-contained Bootstrap HTML report from any objects (contains embedded JavaScript)

### Feature folders
`applications`, `auditLogs`, `devices`, `domains`, `groups`, `reports`, `roleManagement`, `servicePrincipals`, `tenantInformation`, `users`.

## Naming Conventions

- **Functions**: `Verb-GtNoun` with the `Gt` prefix for all public functions (e.g., `Get-GtUser`, `Find-GtGroup`). Approved verbs: `Get-` (retrieval), `Find-` (search), `New-`, `Add-`/`Remove-` (mutations), `Disable-`, `Revoke-`, `Invoke-` (actions), `Sync-`, `ConvertTo-`. Small validators/helpers may be lowerCamelCase without prefix (`isValidGuid`).
- **Aliases**: short lowerCamelCase for interactive use, declared with `[Alias('...')]` above `[CmdletBinding()]` (e.g., `userSearch`/`searchUser`, `signInLogs`, `authMethods`, `generateTap`, `chunk`).
- **Files**: one function per file, file name = function name. Exceptions: tightly coupled private helpers can live in the same file (`Invoke-GtGraphSingleBatchRequest`, `storageProviders.ps1`).
- **Parameters**: PascalCase, full names, no abbreviations. (A few older functions use camelCase such as `inputObject`, `outputType`, `skipMembershipCheck`, `objectIdOnly` - keep existing names for compatibility, use PascalCase for new parameters.) Primary input is `-InputObject` (position 0, `ValueFromPipeline`); the common search parameter is `-SearchString`; extra select properties use `-AdditionalProperties`.
- **Private nested helpers**: lowerCamelCase or `Verb-Noun` without `Gt`, defined inside the owning function (e.g., `isPrivilegedPermission`, `Resolve-IdToName`).

---

## Code Style

- 4-space indentation; spaces inside condition parentheses and one-liner braces: `if ( $x ) { ... }`, `catch { throw $_ }`.
- Compact one-line guards: `if ( -not $InputObject ) { throw "input object is null or empty." }`.
- Comments are short, lowercase and explain *why* (`# beta required for authenticationDetails`); use `# todo ...` for known gaps. Group long functions with `#region name` / `#endregion name`.
- Build Graph queries as a splatted hashtable (see pattern 3). Use `return` explicitly.
- **Errors**: `throw` for fatal errors (descriptive message, include `$_` from the inner failure); `Write-Warning` for non-fatal problems (duplicates, skipped items, optional data unavailable); `Write-Host` only for user-facing status of interactive actions.
- **Verbose/debug**: `Write-GtVerbose "..."` for progress; `Write-Debug` for per-item detail. Pass `-Verbose:$false` to inner `Invoke-GtGraphRequest` calls to keep verbose output readable.
- **Progress**: `Write-Progress` only for long-running loops (batching); always finish with `-Completed`.

---

## Key Patterns

### 1. Input Flexibility
Accept UPN, GUID, or objects with `id`/`userPrincipalName`, support the pipeline, resolve with `idFromInputObject`:

```powershell
function Get-GtUser {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param (
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipeline = $true, Position = 0)]
        [Object]$InputObject
    )
    process {
        $id = idFromInputObject -inputObject $InputObject | Select-Object -ExpandProperty id
        try { return Invoke-GtGraphRequest -resourcePath "users/$id" -select "id,displayName" }
        catch { throw $_ }
    }
}

# All valid:
Get-GtUser "user@contoso.com"
Get-GtUser "guid-here"
$user | Get-GtUser
```

- Use `-objectIdOnly` where Graph requires an object ID (group/member mutations); those functions document that display names/UPNs are not accepted.

### 2. Reads: Invoke-GtGraphRequest; Writes: Invoke-MgGraphRequest
```powershell
# ✅ Reads - auto-pagination, OData params, dateTimes converted to local time
$users = Invoke-GtGraphRequest -resourcePath "users" -select "id,displayName" -filter "accountEnabled eq true"

# ❌ Wrong for reads - manual pagination, no dateTime conversion
$users = Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri "..."
```
`Invoke-GtGraphRequest` has no `-Method`, so POST/PATCH/DELETE call `Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method ... -OutputType PSObject` directly (use `-StatusCodeVariable` when the status matters, e.g. 204). Wrap the call in `try { } catch { throw $_ }`.

**Always convert dateTimes** from direct `Invoke-MgGraphRequest` responses (`Invoke-GtGraphRequest` and `Invoke-GtGraphBatchRequest` already do it):
```powershell
$null = ConvertTo-GtLocalDateTime -InputObject $response   # in place; discard output to keep the response shape
```

### 3. OData Parameters with Splatting
```powershell
$params = @{
    resourcePath = "users"
    apiVersion   = "beta"  # or "v1.0" (default)
    select       = "id,displayName,signInActivity"
    filter       = "userType eq 'Member'"
    expand       = "manager(`$select=displayName)"
}
if ( $AdditionalProperties ) { $params.select = "$($params.select),$AdditionalProperties" }
$users = Invoke-GtGraphRequest @params
```
- `-search` values must be quoted inside the string (e.g. `'"displayName:john"'`); the ConsistencyLevel header is added automatically for `-search`/`-count`.
- Use `-apiVersion beta` only when required (e.g., `signInActivity`, `authenticationDetails`) and add a comment why.

### 4. Batch Processing
```powershell
$requests = $ids | ForEach-Object {
    @{ id = $_; method = "GET"; url = "users/$_" }   # relative url, no leading slash, id must be unique
}
$results = Invoke-GtGraphBatchRequest -Requests $requests -ApiVersion v1.0
$results[$someId]   # hashtable keyed by request id; value is the response body (or .value)
```
Use batching for multiple per-object calls (relationships such as owners/sponsors, auth methods). `select` is not supported on directoryObject relationship URLs.

### 5. Mutating Functions: -WhatIf / -Confirm (CLM-safe)
Destructive functions implement their own preview and confirmation (no `ShouldProcess`):

```powershell
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipeline = $true, Position = 0)]
    [Object]$InputObject,
    [switch]$WhatIf,
    [bool]$Confirm = $true
)
process {
    # confirm (constrained language mode does not support ShouldProcess)
    if ( $Confirm -and -not $WhatIf ) {
        $confirmation = Read-Host "Revoke all sessions for user '$id'? (Y/N)"
        if ( $confirmation -ne "Y" -and $confirmation -ne "y" ) { Write-Host "Operation cancelled." -ForegroundColor Yellow; return }
    }
    if ( $WhatIf ) { Write-Host "WhatIf: Would revoke all sessions for user '$id'" -ForegroundColor Yellow; return }
    ...
}
```
- Colors: Yellow = WhatIf/cancelled/skipped, Green = success, Red = disabled/removed.
- Return a result object (`userId`, `success`, `timestamp`) built with `New-Object PSObject` + `Add-Member` when the caller may need it.
- Document `-WhatIf` and `-Confirm` in `.PARAMETER`; mention `-Confirm $false` / `-Confirm:$false` for automation in an example.

### 6. Reports
Report functions in `src/reports/` return **either** objects **or** an HTML report:
- Switch `-Raw` (enriched objects, IDs retained) or `-outputType PSObject|html` (default `html`).
- HTML via `Export-GtHtmlReport -InputObject ... -ReportTitle ... -TitleProperty ... -Path ".\PSGraphToolbox_<Name>_$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd_HHmmss').html"`.
- Fetch optional/privileged data in `try/catch` and degrade with `Write-Warning "<Function>: <thing> unavailable."` plus an empty hashtable, rather than failing the whole report.
- Resolve IDs to names in bulk (`Get-GtGraphDirectoryObjectsByIds` -> `ConvertTo-HashTable`) instead of per-object calls.

### 7. Lookup Tables
Convert arrays to hashtables with `ConvertTo-HashTable -keyProperty "id"` for O(1) joins instead of `Where-Object` in loops.

## Comment-Based Help Guidelines

**Every function needs help - including private nested helpers.** Scale help to complexity: simple functions need minimal help; complex functions need detailed examples.

### Critical Formatting Rules
- **Keywords (e.g., `.EXAMPLE`) and their content must be at the SAME indentation level - no extra tabs/spaces before the description text.**
- **The help block must be the first thing in the function body** (directly after `function Name {`). A comment (e.g. `# todo`) above the help block makes PowerShell/platyPS ignore it - put such comments after `param()`/below the help.
- Use `<# ... #>` with `.SYNOPSIS` etc. Single-line `<# text #>` comments are **not** help.
- Place help inside the function (indented 4 spaces), before `[Alias()]`/`[CmdletBinding()]`/`param`.

```powershell
function Get-GtUser {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Retrieves a user from Microsoft Entra ID

    .DESCRIPTION
    Accepts flexible input (UPN, GUID, or object) and returns user details.
    Requires scopes: User.Read.All

    .PARAMETER InputObject
    User identifier (UPN, GUID, or object with id/userPrincipalName)

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-GtUser "user@contoso.com"
    Retrieves user by UPN

    .EXAMPLE
    $user | Get-GtUser -AdditionalProperties "department"
    Pipeline usage with extra properties

    .LINK
    https://github.com/alflokken/PSGraphToolbox/blob/main/docs/users/Get-GtUser.md
    #>
```

### What to Include

**Simple functions (5-20 lines):**
- `.SYNOPSIS` - one sentence
- `.DESCRIPTION` - required scopes, brief explanation
- `.PARAMETER` - **for every declared parameter**, including `-WhatIf`/`-Confirm`, `-Raw`, `-Verbose`-style switches (parameter names are matched case-insensitively)
- `.EXAMPLE` - 1-2 examples, each followed by a line describing the result

**Complex functions (20+ lines, multiple params):**
- Same as above, plus:
- More `.EXAMPLE` entries showing different use cases (pipeline, `-WhatIf`, output filtering)
- `.NOTES` if special considerations exist (API limitations, token refresh, etc.)
- `.OUTPUTS` when the output shape isn't obvious (list the returned properties)

**Always include:**
- `.LINK` for every **top-level (exported)** function - link to the generated documentation:
  ```
  .LINK
  https://github.com/alflokken/PSGraphToolbox/blob/main/docs/{category}/{FunctionName}.md
  ```
  Where `{category}` is the immediate parent folder name of the source file (e.g., `auditLogs`, `core`, `helpers`, `storageProviders`).
- Private nested functions get `.SYNOPSIS`, `.PARAMETER` and `.EXAMPLE`, but **no `.LINK`** (no docs page is generated for them).

**Don't include:**
- `PS>` prompt in examples - causes rendering issues
- Raw output after commands - describe the result in text instead
- `.INPUTS` if obvious from context

### Required Permissions
Document in `.DESCRIPTION` as a separate line; list every scope the function needs, and mark optional ones:

```powershell
.DESCRIPTION
Retrieves conditional access policies.

Requires scopes: Policy.Read.All
Optional: AuditLog.Read.All (-IncludeSignInActivity)
```

### Keep help in sync
When changing parameters, defaults or output, update `.PARAMETER`, examples and `.OUTPUTS` in the same change (defaults in help must match the `param` block). Also update `README.md` when user-facing behavior changes.

## Testing

- Pester tests live in `tests/`; every file starts with `#Requires -Module Pester` and imports the built module in `BeforeAll`: `Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\PsGraphToolbox.psd1") -Force`. **Rebuild the module (`utils\build.ps1`) before testing `src/` changes** - tests run against the generated `.psm1`.
- `Core.Tests.ps1` / `Helpers.Unit.Tests.ps1`: offline unit tests for pure functions and mocked core behavior. `Graph.Integration.Tests.ps1`: tagged `-Tag 'Integration'`, needs a live Graph connection and read-only scopes.
- Structure with `#region <Function> Tests` + `Describe '<Function>'` + `It 'Should ...'`.
- Run: `Invoke-Pester -Path .\tests\Helpers.Unit.Tests.ps1 -Output Detailed` (PowerShell 5.1).

## Common Code Patterns

### Resolve GUIDs to Names
```powershell
$guidList = $policy.conditions.users.includeUsers
$names = Get-GtGraphDirectoryObjectsByIds -Type user -Ids $guidList | Select-Object -ExpandProperty displayName
# for many lookups, build a hashtable once: ... | ConvertTo-HashTable
```

### Date Filtering
```powershell
$date = (Get-Date).AddDays(-30).ToUniversalTime().ToString("yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ")
$filter = "createdDateTime ge $date"
```
Graph returns UTC; `Invoke-GtGraphRequest` converts results to local time, so send UTC and display local.

### Progress Reporting
```powershell
$total = $items.Count
$current = 0
foreach ($item in $items) {
    $current++
    Write-Progress -Activity "Processing" -Status "$current of $total" -PercentComplete (($current / $total) * 100)
}
Write-Progress -Activity "Processing" -Completed
```

---

## Performance Tips

1. **Use `$select`** - Only request needed properties
2. **Use batch API** - For multiple individual requests (20 per batch)
3. **Server-side filter** - Use `$filter` not `Where-Object`
4. **Bulk resolve IDs** - `Get-GtGraphDirectoryObjectsByIds` (1000 per call) + `ConvertTo-HashTable`
5. **Avoid `+=` on large arrays** - collect via pipeline/`foreach` output where possible

```powershell
# ❌ Slow
$all = Invoke-GtGraphRequest -resourcePath "users"
$active = $all | Where-Object accountEnabled

# ✅ Fast
$active = Invoke-GtGraphRequest -resourcePath "users" -filter "accountEnabled eq true" -select "id,displayName,userPrincipalName"
```
